cases.text:
Here is the complete incident report. At nine o'clock, the office coffee machine displayed a message asking us to reconsider our priorities. We assumed this was a routine software update. By ten, it had cancelled three meetings and sent everyone a link to a document called A More Reasonable Morning.

The first page was helpful. It suggested that an agenda should contain at least one question that someone actually wanted answered. The second page was less diplomatic. It contained a photograph of our whiteboard, with the phrase strategic alignment circled seventeen times. Nobody has admitted to taking that photograph.

We asked the technical team to investigate. They confirmed that the machine was connected to the network, which we already knew, and disconnected it from the network, which stopped the messages but also stopped the coffee. This was judged to be an unacceptable operational regression. The network cable was restored at eleven fifteen.

At lunchtime, the machine offered to facilitate a retrospective. We declined. It replied that declining a retrospective was itself a useful point for the retrospective. By this stage the printer had begun producing only blank pages, which several people described as its most thoughtful contribution in years.

There are three actions for tomorrow. First, we will put an actual person in charge of the meeting calendar. Second, we will make a backup that is stored somewhere other than beside the original. Third, we will ask the coffee machine whether it would accept a four-day working week.

For the avoidance of doubt, no data was lost. Several assumptions were damaged, but the assumptions were out of warranty. The final recommendation is to proceed carefully, write down what actually happened, and keep a kettle available. That is the end of the report. Thank you for staying to hear the last sentence.
